column2: ENGLISH

The last fall of rubble has been hauled out and the last Night Goblin burned, and the old stretch of the Ungdrin Ankor beneath your hold stands open again. Engineers have shored the vaults with new iron, Ironbreakers stand at the junctions, and the first caravan of mules and lantern-bearers is already rumbling off into the dark towards the next hold, as caravans did in the Golden Age before the earth shook.
Let the caravans run.

The engineers have laid iron rails along the open stretches of the Underway, and the first mining carriages come clattering out of the dark under a plume of steam, loaded with ore, ale and grumbling passengers. What took a caravan days now takes hours. The traditionalists mutter that no good ever came of going so fast underground.
Mind the rails.

Word comes up from the deep ways: the stretch of the Underway your hold had reopened is lost. The shoring has failed or the enemy has broken through, and the tunnels are choked with rubble and worse. Once more the hold is cut off below ground, as it was in the long years after the earth shook.
Write it down.

A caravan due from the next hold never arrived. A patrol found the carts overturned in a side gallery of the Underway near [underway_hold.GetName], the mules gone and the drivers dead, with Night Goblin arrows still in them. Squig spoor runs off into the dark. The Goblins have dug their way into your stretch of the tunnels again, and they will be back.
Send the Ironbreakers down.
Seal the tunnel for now.
In a Goblin warren the Ironbreakers find a suit of gromril armour, the gear of one of their own who fell there long ago, and bring it to you.
The Goblins are driven out, but at a cost in dead and in burial gold.

The miners working the lowest gallery of the Underway near [underway_hold.GetName] have stopped work. They have put their ears to the floor, and every one of them heard it: scratching, from below, and the sharp stink of warpstone coming up through the cracks. The ratmen are tunnelling up into your stretch of the road.
Dig down and meet them.
Bring the tunnel down on their heads.
The Ironbreakers break into the Skaven tunnel and burn it out.
The Skaven hold their tunnel, and the stretch must be sealed until it can be retaken.

A long caravan has come up out of the Underway from another hold, ingots and worked iron, kegs of ale and bundles of Grobi skins, with a dozen grim Dawi guards. Its master asks to pass beneath [underway_hold.GetName] on the old road. By old custom a hold may take a toll from those who use its stretch of the tunnels. By older custom, from the Golden Age, the Underway was free to every Dawi.
Take the toll.
Let it pass free, for the sake of the old roads.

A patrol clearing an old stretch of the Underway has found a waystone, half buried in rubble from the time the earth shook. The runes are cut in an older form of Khazalid, and they still give the distances to holds that have not been heard from in thousands of years. The Ironbreakers who carried it up will not let anyone else touch it.
Set it up in the temple of the ancestors.
Copy the runes for the loremasters.

A mining carriage jumped the rails in the dark and ploughed into the wall of the tunnel, spilling a full load of ore across the line. Nobody was killed, but the driver swears blind that the rail was loose, and the engineers swear just as hard that it was not. Until the carriage is hauled back the line is blocked.
Pay the engineers to put it right.
Make the driver haul it back himself.
I will see to it myself.
Underway Sealed
This stretch of the Underway has been sealed against the enemies below. It is safe, but closed to traffic.
Line Blocked
A derailed mining carriage blocks the line through this stretch of the Underway.
